text: Analysis tells you how a program scales and measurement tells you what it costs today. A recursion whose depth grows with the input has a limit far below what memory suggests, because recursion depth is ___ complexity.
explanation: Chapter 12 measured this machine's stack at about 20,000 frames, so a recursive walk of a hundred-thousand-element list overflows where the iterative version does not. A recursion of depth log n — divide and conquer — is fine forever, since the logarithm of anything is small. That is one of the more useful practical consequences of taking space seriously alongside time.
